      {\small\bfseries\color{AccentBlue}IMAGE PLACEHOLDER}\par
      \vspace{0.12cm}
      {\small\color{Ink}#2\par}
      \vspace{0.10cm}
      {\scriptsize\ttfamily\color{Muted}\detokenize{#3}\par}%
    };
  \end{tikzpicture}\par
}

% ----- SLIDE 5 (original NVIDIA slide 2): technology mapping background -----
\begin{frame}{What Is Technology Mapping?}
  \vspace{0.07cm}
  \smalllabel{01 / Background}\par
  \vspace{0.08cm}
  {\small\color{Muted}From a technology-independent Boolean network to a standard-cell implementation.}
  \vspace{-0.16cm}
  \begin{center}
    % Slide 2: the existing AIGmapping.png from your Overleaf project.
    \includegraphics[width=\linewidth,height=4.45cm,keepaspectratio,
        trim=0 155bp 0 119bp,clip]{AIGmapping.png}%
  \end{center}
  \vspace{-0.03cm}
  \takeaway{Choose library cells to preserve logic and optimize area and delay.}
  \vspace{0.10cm}
  {\normalsize\bfseries\color{Ink}Result: a mapped gate-level netlist for downstream Physical Design (placement and routing).\par}
\end{frame}

% ----- SLIDE 6 (original NVIDIA slide 3): motivation -----
% Side-by-side comparisons use uploaded SO_mapping.png and MO_mapping.png.
% The PNG headings/extra whitespace are cropped, as the slide adds badges.
% Both figures include surrounding upstream and downstream logic; only the
% highlighted region changes from SO cells to a single multi-output cell.
% The ASAP7 FA example uses inverted SN and CON outputs.
\begin{frame}{Why Consider Multi-Output Cells?}
  \vspace{0.05cm}
  \smalllabel{02 / Motivation}
  \vspace{0.12cm}
  \takeaway{Single-output mapping may miss joint implementations.}
  \vspace{-0.25cm}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.492\textwidth}
      \minibadge{SoftLilac}{Single-output cell mapping}
      \vspace{0.02cm}
      \begin{center}
        \includegraphics[width=\linewidth,height=3.95cm,keepaspectratio,trim=0 105bp 0 250bp,clip]{SO_mapping.png}
      \end{center}
      \vspace{-0.18cm}
      % The SO circuit diagram already illustrates the separate-cell implementation.
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.492\textwidth}
      \minibadge{SoftMint}{Multi-output cell mapping}
      \vspace{0.02cm}
      \begin{center}
        \includegraphics[width=\linewidth,height=3.95cm,keepaspectratio,trim=0 180bp 0 175bp,clip]{MO_mapping.png}
      \end{center}
      \vspace{-0.18cm}
      % The MO circuit diagram already illustrates the joint-cell implementation.
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  \vspace{-0.16cm}
  \begin{center}
    {\small\bfseries\color{Accent}Potential benefit: }
    {\small\color{Ink}One multi-output cell can reduce area and delay versus separate single-output cells.}
  \end{center}
\end{frame}

% ----- SLIDE 7 (original NVIDIA slide 4): proposed mapping framework -----

% Slide 8's 30-case QoR results come from the earlier bridge-based evaluation.
\begin{frame}{Proposed Mapping Framework}
  \vspace{0.06cm}
  \smalllabel{03 / Framework}\par
  \vspace{0.10cm}
  \takeaway{Extend ABC with multi-output candidate discovery and output-pair binding.}
  \vspace{-0.08cm}
  \begin{center}
    \includegraphics[width=\linewidth,height=4.70cm,keepaspectratio,
        trim=0 80bp 0 132bp,clip]{MappingFramework.png}%
  \end{center}
\end{frame}

% ----- SLIDE 8 (original NVIDIA slide 5): new independent MO match discovery -----
% Both SO and MO use cut-based search, but the new MO search stores its
% cuts separately and retains candidates matching MO output roles.
\begin{frame}{New Multi-Output Match Discovery}
  \vspace{0.03cm}
  \smalllabel{04 / Candidate Discovery}\par
  \vspace{0.12cm}
  \takeaway{SO-oriented cut pruning may miss matches useful for multi-output cells.}
  \vspace{0.02cm}
  \begin{center}
  \begin{tikzpicture}[>=Latex, font=\small, line width=0.65pt]
    \tikzset{
      soStep/.style={draw=AccentBlue!60,fill=white,rounded corners=2pt,
        text width=4.82cm,minimum height=.83cm,inner xsep=3.5pt,
        inner ysep=2pt,align=center},
      moStep/.style={draw=Accent!60,fill=white,rounded corners=2pt,
        text width=4.82cm,minimum height=.83cm,inner xsep=3.5pt,
        inner ysep=2pt,align=center}
    }
    \fill[SoftBlue!65,rounded corners=4pt] (-6.00,-0.52) rectangle (-0.24,3.16);
    \draw[AccentBlue!55,rounded corners=4pt] (-6.00,-0.52) rectangle (-0.24,3.16);
    \fill[SoftMint!70,rounded corners=4pt] (0.24,-0.52) rectangle (6.00,3.16);
    \draw[Accent!55,rounded corners=4pt] (0.24,-0.52) rectangle (6.00,3.16);
    \node[font=\bfseries\small,text=Ink] at (-3.12,2.78) {Existing SO Enumeration};
    \node[font=\bfseries\small,text=Ink] at (3.12,2.78) {New MO Match Discovery};
    \node[soStep]
      (so1) at (-3.12,2.03) {Cut enumeration};
    \node[moStep]
      (mo1) at (3.12,2.03) {Independent cut enumeration};
    \node[soStep]
      (so2) at (-3.12,1.08) {SO-oriented area / delay pruning};
    \node[moStep]
      (mo2) at (3.12,1.08) {Boolean matching to\\MO output roles};
    \draw[AccentBlue,->,thick] (so1.south) -- (so2.north);
    \draw[Accent,->,thick] (mo1.south) -- (mo2.north);
    \node[soStep]
      (so3) at (-3.12,0.13) {SO matches};
    \node[moStep]
      (mo3) at (3.12,0.13) {Role-aware cut retention};
    \draw[AccentBlue,->,thick] (so2.south) -- (so3.north);
    \draw[Accent,->,thick] (mo2.south) -- (mo3.north);
    \node[font=\scriptsize\itshape,text=Muted,anchor=north]
      at (-3.12,-.68) {Some MO-useful cuts may be pruned};
    \node[font=\scriptsize\bfseries,text=Accent,anchor=north]
      at (3.12,-.68) {Preserve output-role matches for pairing};
  \end{tikzpicture}
  \end{center}
  \vspace{-0.21cm}
  {\small\color{Muted}The existing SO enumeration remains unchanged; new MO cuts are kept separately.\par}
\end{frame}

% ----- SLIDE 9 (original NVIDIA slide 6): output-pair binding and legality -----
% sharedLeaves.png illustrates two independently matched AIG cut cones
% with the same shared support. MOCnadidate.png is a LEGAL CANDIDATE,
% not the final cell selection; optimization decides that on Slide 7.
\begin{frame}{Output-Pair Binding \& Legality}
  \vspace{0.02cm}
  \smalllabel{05 / Candidate Integration}\par
  \vspace{0.09cm}
  \takeaway{Two matched outputs need compatible pins and a safely replaceable SO cover.}
  \vspace{-0.05cm}
  \begin{columns}[c,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.30\textwidth}
      \begin{center}
        \includegraphics[width=\linewidth,height=4.40cm,keepaspectratio,
          trim=0 40bp 0 0bp,clip]{sharedLeaves.png}%
      \end{center}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.385\textwidth}
      \vspace{0.27cm}
      {\scriptsize\bfseries\color{Accent}01 \quad Shared support \& pin mapping}\par
      \vspace{0.05cm}
      {\small\color{Ink}Same cut leaves; compatible pin configuration.}\par
      \vspace{0.26cm}
      {\scriptsize\bfseries\color{Accent}02 \quad Structural legality}\par
      \vspace{0.05cm}
      {\small\color{Ink}No dependency between output roots.}\par
      \vspace{0.26cm}
      {\scriptsize\bfseries\color{Accent}03 \quad SO replacement witness}\par
      \vspace{0.05cm}
      {\small\color{Ink}Find a safely replaceable SO subcover.}\par
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.285\textwidth}
      \vspace{0.33cm}
      \begin{center}
        \includegraphics[width=\linewidth,height=3.45cm,keepaspectratio,
          trim=0 12bp 0 0bp,clip]{MOCnadidate.png}%
      \end{center}
      \vspace{-0.06cm}
      {\centering\scriptsize\color{Accent}Candidate only; final mapping is selected later.\par}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  \vspace{-0.14cm}
  {\small\bfseries\color{Ink}Result: a legal MO binding, ready for joint SO/MO optimization.\par}
\end{frame}

% ----- SLIDE 10 (original NVIDIA slide 7): differentiable SO/MO binding decision -----
% Decision graph is optimizer-side control, not an AIG/timing node.
% SO: each endpoint root independently selects from its SO match candidates.
% MO: one physical cell drives both endpoint roots.
% Crop the image's embedded title and bottom summary; retain central graph.
\begin{frame}{Joint SO/MO Mapping Decision}
  \vspace{0.02cm}
  \smalllabel{06 / Differentiable Optimization}\par
  \vspace{-0.16cm}
  \begin{center}
    \includegraphics[width=\linewidth,height=6.00cm,keepaspectratio,
        trim=8bp 116bp 8bp 138bp,clip]{mapper.png}%
  \end{center}
  \vspace{-0.19cm}
  % Soft: differentiable probabilities optimized through continuous relaxation.
  % Hard: argmax over SO/MO branch scores gives a one-hot decision.
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.59\textwidth}
      {\small\bfseries\color{Ink}Soft: optimize differentiable SO/MO probabilities.\par}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.39\textwidth}
      {\small\bfseries\color{Ink}Hard: argmax $\rightarrow$ one-hot selection.\par}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  \vspace{0.00cm}
  {\small\color{Muted}Physical model: count MO area once; evaluate timing at each output pin.\par}
\end{frame}

% ----- SLIDE 12 (original NVIDIA slide 9): software engineering, correctness, and scalability -----
% Independent ABC MO discovery and end-to-end validation.
% N = AIG nodes, C = maximum retained MO cuts/node.
% O(C^2) counts cut-pair attempts at binary nodes; O(NC) is retained-pool storage.
\begin{frame}{Software Engineering: Correctness \& Scalability}
  \vspace{0.02cm}
  \smalllabel{08 / Implementation \& Testing}\par
  \vspace{0.03cm}
  \setbeamercolor{engleft}{fg=Ink,bg=SoftBlue!58}
  \setbeamercolor{engright}{fg=Ink,bg=SoftMint!62}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.485\textwidth}
      \begin{beamercolorbox}[rounded=true,sep=0.17cm,wd=\linewidth]{engleft}
        {\large\bfseries\color{AccentBlue}Correctness \& Testing}\par
        \vspace{0.06cm}
        {\normalsize\bfseries Smoke Regression}\par
        {\small Small circuit benchmarks after\\ code changes.}\par
        \vspace{0.05cm}
        {\color{Divider}\rule{\dimexpr\linewidth-0.36cm\relax}{0.55pt}}\par
        \vspace{0.06cm}
        {\normalsize\bfseries CEC Verification}\par
        {\small Combinational Equivalence Checking:\par
        input logic function vs.\par
        mapped netlist function.}\par
        \vspace{0.05cm}
        {\color{Divider}\rule{\dimexpr\linewidth-0.36cm\relax}{0.55pt}}\par
        \vspace{0.06cm}
        {\normalsize\bfseries Three-Stage Validation}\par
        {\small {\color{AccentBlue}\bfseries 1.}\quad SO mapping regression\par
        {\color{AccentBlue}\bfseries 2.}\quad MO Boolean \& structural checks\par
        {\color{AccentBlue}\bfseries 3.}\quad Netlist generation + CEC.}\par
        \vspace{0.01cm}
      \end{beamercolorbox}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.485\textwidth}
      \begin{beamercolorbox}[rounded=true,sep=0.17cm,wd=\linewidth]{engright}
        {\large\bfseries\color{Accent}Complexity \& Scalability}\par
        \vspace{0.06cm}
        {\normalsize\bfseries Cut Enumeration}\par
        {\small Binary node: $O(C^{2})$ cut-pair attempts.\par Retained-cut storage: $O(NC)$.}\par
        \vspace{0.05cm}
        {\color{Divider}\rule{\dimexpr\linewidth-0.36cm\relax}{0.55pt}}\par
        \vspace{0.06cm}
        {\normalsize\bfseries Search-Space Limits}\par
        {\small $K=3$ maximum leaves; $C=128$ retained MO cuts per node.}\par
        \vspace{0.05cm}
        {\color{Divider}\rule{\dimexpr\linewidth-0.36cm\relax}{0.55pt}}\par
        \vspace{0.06cm}
        {\normalsize\bfseries Runtime \& Memory Control}\par
        {\small Early pruning and deduplication;\par
        runtime and peak-memory monitoring.}\par
        \vspace{0.01cm}
      \end{beamercolorbox}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}
